name: Antipaladin Soul Eater
body:
Antipaladins are scions of evil, spreading fear and cruelty in their wake. Souleaters do so in a different way. Instead of instilling fear and degradation in others, they absorb their life and souls to empower themselves.

Draining Strike (Su)

Beginning at 1st level, the soul eater channels vile energy through their weapons to drain the life force from their targets. On a successful hit, as a swift action, the soul eater can add 1d6 damage per two class levels to the damage dealt by their attack.

This only affects creatures with souls, so automata and objects are not affected. The extra damage dealt is not multiplied on a critical hit. The soul eater gains temporary hit points equal to the extra damage dealt.

The temporary hit points do not stack and they expire after 1 hour. This ability is usable a number of times per day equal to 1/2 their class level + their Charisma modifier. A successful Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the soul eater’s class level + their Charisma modifier) halves the damage and the temporary hit points provided.

This ability replaces smite good and touch of corruption.

Steal Power (Su)

Beginning at 3rd level, the soul eater can sap the power from a target with their draining strike. Instead of the damage and temporary hit points, the soul eater can choose to impose a Strength or Intelligence penalty. The Strength penalty can only target creatures that have a corporeal body and can be targeted by draining strike. The Intelligence penalty can only target creatures that are not mindless and can be targeted by draining strike. In either case the target takes a -2 penalty. The penalty increases by 1 every three levels after 3rd level. The penalty cannot reduce the target’s effective ability score below 1. The soul eater gains an enhancement bonus to the same ability score equal to the penalty imposed. The penalty imposed and the enhancement bonus last for 1 minute per class level, or until the soul eater is reduced to 0 hit points. A successful saving throw on the part of the target halves the penalty imposed and enhancement bonus granted, and reduces the duration to 1 round per class level or until the soul eater is reduced to 0 hit points. The saving throw against the Strength penalty is Fortitude while the saving throw against the Intelligence penalty is Will. The DC for the Fortitude save is the same as the Will save for draining strike.

This ability replaces aura of cowardice and the cruelty granted at 3rd level.

Draining Ray (Su)

Beginning at 4th level, the soul eater can gain the effects of draining strike, or any abilities that use draining strike like steal power, with a ray of dark energy. The soul eater does not deal their weapon damage in this circumstance, only the additional effect. The ray requires a ranged touch attack, takes a standard action, and has a range of 60 feet. The ray must otherwise adhere to the requirements of the ability used.

This ability replaces channel energy.

Steal Vitality (Su)

Beginning at 7th level, the soul eater gains the ability to drain the target’s vitality. This ability functions as steal power but allows the soul eater to impose a penalty to, and gain an enhancement bonus from, the target’s Constitution or Wisdom. The Constitution effect can only target living creatures and the Wisdom effect cannot target creatures immune to mind-affecting effects. The saving throw for the Constitution effect is Fortitude and the saving throw for the Wisdom effect is Will.

This ability replaces the cruelty gained at 6th level and aura of despair.

Steal Vigor (Su)

Beginning at 10th level, the soul eater gains the ability to drain the target’s mental and physical agility. This ability functions as steal power but allows the soul eater to impose a penalty to, and gain an enhancement bonus from, the target’s Dexterity or Charisma. The saving throw for the Dexterity effect is Fortitude and the saving throw for the Charisma effect is Will.

This ability replaces the cruelty gained at 9th level and aura of vengeance.

Empty Shell (Su)

Beginning at 12th level, the soul eater can turn a drained, empty husk of a creature into a terrible monstrosity. If the soul eater kills a living target with the damage from their draining strike or drain energy abilities, they can raise the target as a wight. This ability does not work in an area of consecrate or if the target has some effect that prevents them from becoming an undead. The wight created is under the soul eater’s control. If the target was undead and reduced to 0 hit points, it is reanimated again but under your control. The Hit Dice of the reanimated creature, wight or other undead, cannot exceed your class level. The soul eater can only have one undead under their control from this ability, if a second undead is reanimated with this ability, the previous undead crumbles to dust.

This ability replaces the cruelties gained at 12th and 18th levels.

Energy Drain (Su)

Beginning at 15th level, the soul eater drains the essence from the target. The soul eater can expend a use of draining strike when activating it to impose one negative level, no saving throw, or two uses of the ability to impose two negative levels. Doing so grants the soul eater the choice of 10 temporary hit points per level drain, or a +2 enhancement bonus to an ability score per level drain. These benefits do not stack with other uses of draining strike or itself and expire after 1 hour.

This ability replaces the cruelty gained at 15th level.

Mastery of Souls (Su)

Beginning at 20th level, the soul eater is a mastery of soul energy. They gain the following benefits:

Temporary hit points granted by any uses of the draining strike ability last for 24 hours.
The steal power, steal vitality and steal vigor abilities penalize both ability scores and grant the soul eater bonuses to both. The target makes the saving throw against the DC for which they have the lower bonus.
For energy drain, they can choose two options for the benefit granted for imposing negative levels.

This ability replaces unholy champion.
